localChanges: Twelve civilizations join Civilization's fourteen: the Sioux, Incas, Brazilians, Malians, Kongolese, Ethiopians, Vikings, Khmer, Indonesians, Japanese, Australians and Chukchi, each with their own leaders, colours and cities (#466).
On Earth, every civilization now starts at least five squares from any other, so close neighbours like England and France no longer share land from the first turn, and the Mongols start in Mongolia.

civ1-world-civilizations gives them to the Australians and the Vikings. Left in the spare list, a civilization that had run out of its own names could take them too, and the game could have two of each.
civ1-science 0.1.5 added FutureTechnology (civ-clone/web-renderer#458), so "grades every Civ1 advance, each once" failed in CI on master too.

Every civilization's Earth start is now placed by `tools/earth-maps/starts.py`, on all three maps: Civilization's own 14 together with the 12 civ1-world-civilizations adds. Each starts from its real capital through the map warp, and takes the nearby Grassland, Plains or River that keeps every start at least 5 tiles from every other, so no two capitals share a city tile. Before, London and Paris shared 7 of their 21 tiles on 80 x 50.
The Mongols move from Samarkand to Karakorum. The original map's terrain is unchanged; only its start tiles move. The plugin's starts are written to `tools/earth-maps/world-civilizations.json`.

From review: the start-tile rewrite now fails loudly instead of leaving the file unchanged, and nothing is written unless all three maps' starts fit. civ1map.py drops its unused STARTS, and the docs say what placing does: it moves starts little, favouring good land, rather than provably least. Regenerating gives the same maps and JSON.

Registers the Sioux, Incas, Brazilians, Malians, Kongolese, Ethiopians, Vikings, Khmer, Indonesians, Japanese, Australians and Chukchi, each from its base-civilization package, with every leader and that leader's Civ1 traits (Mood, Policy, Ideology) for civ1-civilization's personality rules. Each gets an Earth start tile at every size, from civ1-earth-generator's tools/earth-maps, at least 5 tiles from any other start.

From review: civ1-civilization/Traits only re-exports library-civilization's, so the plugin takes them from there and civ1-civilization is now just a dev dependency (for the city-name test). The tests now check each civilization, leader and Earth start tile is registered exactly once, and that none of the 12 civilizations' city names is one of Civ1's spare names (Sydney, Melbourne and Bergen were, until civ-clone/civ1-civilization#5). The README says what leaving the package out does.
